title: Training & Education
metaDescription: Cybersecurity training for facility and operations personnel, built for the roles that actually touch OT/ICS systems, not generic awareness content.
heroDek: Generic phishing-awareness training doesn't tell a control-room operator what to do when a screen behaves strangely. This training is built for the roles that actually touch the systems.
contextHeading: The people closest to the control systems are rarely the audience generic training was built for
contextParagraphs: Most commercial cybersecurity training is written for office IT users, covering how to recognize a phishing email, choose a strong password, and report a suspicious link. That content has a place, but it doesn't address the roles that matter most in a converged OT environment, such as the control-room operator who notices a system behaving unexpectedly, the engineer making a change to a control-system network, or the security team member who has to decide whether an anomaly warrants escalation.

GSS builds cybersecurity training around those roles specifically, covering what to notice, what to report, and how a given decision fits into the facility's broader incident response process. It's designed to complement, not duplicate, the physical-security and tactical training GSS also delivers, so personnel understand where cyber awareness fits alongside the security responsibilities they already carry.

Training is delivered at the depth the role requires, with general awareness for the broader workforce, deeper technical content for engineering and IT/OT staff, and decision-focused content for the people who will actually be making a call during a live event.

faq.q: How is this different from the physical/tactical training GSS also offers?
faq.a: That training builds physical-security and response skills. This builds the cybersecurity awareness and decision-making relevant to each role, and is designed to complement the physical-side program rather than repeat it.

faq.q: Is this generic security-awareness content, or built around our systems?
faq.a: It's built around the facility's actual systems, roles, and incident response process, not a generic module set.

faq.q: Can training be delivered to a mixed audience of IT, OT, and operations staff?
faq.a: Yes. Content is tiered by role within a single program, so each audience gets material at the depth relevant to them.
